speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to help me assess your condition, please describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis (likely exacerbated by overuse from holding an infant and a prior fall), with possible concurrent distal radioulnar joint issues. The symptoms of pain in the thumb and wrist radiating to the elbow, worsening with lifting/holding, and relief with ice are classic. The family history of autoimmune joint pain is noted but less likely to be the primary cause given the specific mechanical aggravating factors. I would recommend an ultrasound or X-ray of the right wrist to rule out fracture or significant soft tissue injury from the fall, and to confirm tenosynovitis.
